prompt: A function $f$ is differentiable everywhere, with $f'(x) > 0$ for $x < 1$, $f'(x) < 0$ for $1 < x < 5$, and $f'(x) > 0$ for $x > 5$. Which statement is true?

choices.label: $f$ has a local maximum at $x = 1$ and a local minimum at $x = 5$.
$f$ has a local minimum at $x = 1$ and a local maximum at $x = 5$.
$f$ has local maxima at both $x = 1$ and $x = 5$.

hint: Positive $f'$ means $f$ is climbing; negative means falling. Picture the graph.

hints.text: Positive $f'$ means $f$ is climbing; negative means falling. Picture the graph.
Up to $x = 1$ the graph rises, then falls until $x = 5$, then rises again. What shape is at $x = 1$? At $x = 5$?
Rising then falling is a peak (local max at $1$); falling then rising is a valley (local min at $5$). Choice A.

explanation: First Derivative Test: where $f'$ changes from $+$ to $-$, $f$ has a local maximum. That happens at $x = 1$.
Where $f'$ changes from $-$ to $+$, $f$ has a local minimum. That happens at $x = 5$.
Choice A. The derivative being zero at a point is not enough — it is the sign CHANGE that creates an extremum.

alternativeExplanations.title: Hike the graph
steps: Walk left to right. For $x < 1$ you are going uphill.
At $x = 1$ the trail turns downhill: you were on a summit. You descend until $x = 5$.
At $x = 5$ it turns uphill again: you were in a valley. Summit at $1$, valley at $5$.
